title: Phase 3 sidecar — components
description: Structured component catalog the Phase-3 (Architecture Modeling) LLM persists at PHASE_END. Consumed by scripts/model/build_threat_model_yaml.py to populate threat-model.yaml[components[]] without re-composing from working memory in Phase 11.

schema_version.description: Sidecar schema version. Bump only on breaking changes; add new fields via additions[] entries.

id.description: Canonical component ID used as component_id in threats[] and dispatch-context filenames. Lowercase + hyphens only.

description.description: 1-3 sentence summary of the component's role and technology stack.

paths.description: Canonical repository-relative glob patterns mapping the component to its source files. Every pattern must stay within the target repository and match at least one existing entry when the component inventory is finalized. Glob semantics: '*' matches within one path segment and never crosses '/', '**' spans any number of segments — so 'pkg/*.java' covers only the files directly in 'pkg', and a component whose sources extend into subdirectories must use 'pkg/**/*.java'. Source of truth for the Phase-9 dirty-set mapping.

tier.description: Three-tier architecture classification used by the heatmap renderer. ≥1 component with tier=data is required when the app uses a database/cache/filestore.

complexity.description: Sizes the STRIDE-analyzer turn budget downstream (MAX_TURNS=22/22/31).

framework.description: Primary framework (spring-boot, express, angular, fastapi, ...); for a data component the storage engine (postgresql, sqlite, mongodb, ...), never the ORM. Optional, shown under the component name in Figure 1.

language.description: Implementation language holding most bytes under `paths`. Set by component finalization from file extensions; producers omit it. Absent for data components.

deployment_zones.description: Network/trust placement of this component. Values come from the canonical access-zone vocabulary in data/actors/default-library.yaml (e.g. internet, dmz, client-device, mobile-device, internal-network, peer-service, prod-env, prod-write-db, ci-cd-runtime, build-pipeline, deployment-pipeline). Phase-3-authored: the analyst maps the recon component_hints[].deployment_zones (from .recon-signals.json) onto its own finalized component set, resolving the recon↔analyst ID mismatch by judgment. Consumed by the deterministic STRIDE-component selection predicate (manifest builder) to derive exposure — NOT a hard-coded count. Empty/absent (or only runtime-only tags like docker-container) = treat as exposure-unknown (fail-safe toward inclusion at every depth, including quick).

capabilities.description: Evidenced security-relevant functions of this component (data/security-capabilities.yaml). A capability is not a finding and carries no risk rating.

handles_sensitive_data.description: Crown-jewel flag: true when the component stores or processes credentials, PII, payment data, or secrets. Phase-3-authored from the component's own role (the analyst already knows this while writing the description). Lets the selection predicate keep a high-value datastore in scope even when it is not directly internet-exposed.

workloads.description: Names of the deployment-topology workloads (.dispatch-context/architecture/topology.json) this component models. Authored by the architecture analyst; every topology workload belongs to a component or to unmodelled_workloads.

workload_zones.description: Platform-qualified network zones of the listed workloads. Derived by component-inventory finalization from the deployment inventory; an authored value never survives. Separate from the canonical deployment_zones vocabulary.

deployment_evidence.description: Where each listed workload is defined in deployment configuration. Derived by component-inventory finalization; lets a component without own source files cite its service definition.

unmodelled_workloads.description: Topology workloads deliberately not modelled as or within a component, each with the reason.

additions.description: Optional cross-phase additions discovered after Phase 3 — usually empty. Reserved for future use; current pipeline does not populate.
